title: Metering Service Equipment Catalogue: Meter Types and Their Capabilities
content:
Lakeshore Power & Light sets one of six meter types at a premise under the **Metering Service**. Each type has a fixed ANSI C12 accuracy class and a fixed set of capabilities, and each is set only where its placement conditions hold.

## Placement conditions by meter type

| Meter type | Where the type is set |
|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | Schedule RS Residential Standard Service or Schedule GS Small General Service, no net energy metering, and the customer's own opt-out election |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | Schedule RS, RT, REV, GS or GST service, single phase |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | Net energy metering required, single phase |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | Business customer, three-phase service, Schedule GS Small General Service or Schedule GST Small General Time-of-Use Service |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | Business customer on Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service |
| Primary Metering Installation | Business customer served at primary voltage on Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service or Schedule LP Large Power Service |

## Capabilities

| Meter type | Accuracy class | Remote disconnect and reconnect | Interval data | Time-of-use registers | Delivered and received registered separately | 15-minute demand register |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.5 | No | None (0 minutes) | No | No | No |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.5 | Yes | 60 minutes | Yes | No | No |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.5 | Yes | 15 minutes | Yes | Yes | No |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.5 | No | 15 minutes | Yes | Yes | No |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.2 | No | 15 minutes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Primary Metering Installation | ANSI C12.20 class 0.2 with instrument transformers | No | 15 minutes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

"Time-of-use registers" means the meter records on-peak, off-peak and super off-peak usage for time-of-use schedules. "Delivered and received registered separately" is the bidirectional registration that net energy metering requires.

## Schedules each type can bill, and installation lead time

| Meter type | Rate schedules the type can bill | Business days from order to earliest installation date |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | Schedules RS and GS | 5 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | Schedules RS, RT, REV, GS and GST | 5 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | Schedules RS, RT, REV, GS and GST with a net energy metering rider | 10 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | Schedules GS and GST | 10 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | Schedule GD | 15 |
| Primary Metering Installation | Schedules GD and LP served at primary voltage | 30 |

## Reading the catalogue

- **Remote switching.** Only the Standard AMI Smart Meter and the AMI Bidirectional Net Meter can disconnect and reconnect service remotely; every other type, the Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter included, cannot.
- **Demand.** Only the AMI Interval Demand Meter and the Primary Metering Installation carry a demand register.
- **Accuracy class.** The two demand-capable types are class 0.2; the other four are class 0.5.
- **Example (hypothetical order date).** A Primary Metering Installation ordered on a Monday with no company holidays in the following six weeks can be installed no earlier than the 30th business day after that Monday.
